messages:
Maria (CS): Quick request - can we make a one-page, customer-facing cheat sheet for surge readiness and renewal triage? Focus on small ops they can do: cache priming, batching knobs, streaming fallback, and simple telemetry checks. CS can hand to eng leads during kickoff and renewal calls.
Sam (SRE): Yep. I can draft. Who's the primary audience - infra engineers or product/PMs?
Maria (CS): Engineering owners & CS technical leads. Keep language prescriptive and include copy-paste snippets. Avoid deep infra jargon. :thumbsup:
Jordan (PM): Add a tiny section: 'What to watch in first 72h' and a one-line cost tradeoff tip. Also a short 'what not to try on day 0' list.
Kyle (Support): Please add the on-call escalation path + a link to the shared dashboard. Customers love an explicit contact flow.
Sam (SRE): Draft below. Feedback welcome. I'll keep each item single-line for readability.
Sam (SRE): 
--- BEGIN CHEAT SHEET DRAFT ---
1) Quick prep (before sending traffic)
- Ensure model version pinned (avoid auto-roll).
- Turn on cache priming for top N intents (N=20). TTL 60-300s depending on churn.
- Warm 1x the expected steady QPS (run low-frequency bursts for 10-15m).

2) Batching recommendations (client-side + server hints)
- Target batch size: 4-16 for short prompts; 1-4 for low-latency chat.
- Max wait (max_wait_ms): 20-100ms depending on latency SLO.
- If you see many singletons, increase client-side coalescing window by +10ms.

3) Streaming & graceful fallback
- Prefer streaming for UX where partial tokens matter.
- If streaming stalls >500ms, client should fallback to non-streaming request with a header: `x-rw-fallback: true`.
- Keep a conservative client-side token timeout (e.g., 3s) and show a progress indicator.

4) Cache priming examples (copy-paste)
- curl example to write cached responses (admin endpoint):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/admin/cache/write \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN\" \
  -d '{\"key\":\"intent:greet:v1\",\"value\":\"Hello!\",\"ttl\":120}'
```
- SDK hint: call `client.prefill(inputs, {ttl: 120})` for critical intents.

5) Observability checklist (first 72h)
- Dashboards to watch: token rate, tail latency p95/p99, cache hit rate, batch size distribution.
- Alert triggers: p99 latency > 1.5x SLO for 10m, cache-hit < 60% for 30m, error rate > 0.5%.
- Quick query: `SELECT avg(batch_size) FROM requests WHERE status='ok'`

6) Renewal risk signals & mitigations
- Signals: repeated high latencies, sudden drop in cache-hit, rising cost per 1k users.
- Mitigations: reduce max context length, enable 4-bit quant model variant, increase batching window, enable prefix caching for repeated prompts.

7) What not to do on day 0
- Do not toggle model versions during initial traffic burst.
- Avoid aggressive global caching changes (keep TTLs conservative).

8) Escalation & play path
- Tier 1: customer support (support@redwood.ai) + Slack #customer-success.
- Tier 2: Sam (SRE) on-call (pager) - include `trace-id` and sample payload.
- If degraded for >30m, open a bridge and mention `incident:surge` tag.

9) Short cost tip
- Running bigger batches reduces per-token cost but increases tail latency; tune batch size while watching p99 latency.

--- END CHEAT SHEET DRAFT ---

Jordan (PM): This is clean. Suggest rename `prefill` -> `cache priming`. Also add a one-line sample 72h playbook: Day 0 observe, Day 1 tune batch & TTL, Day 2 cost review + rollback plan.
Kyle (Support): Can we add a link to the standardized dashboard and a small widget customers can copy into their Grafana? Even a JSON snippet.
Sam (SRE): Good call. I'll add a tiny grafana JSON in next iteration and replace the admin curl with a single SDK snippet for JS & Python.
Maria (CS): Love it. Once updated I'll convert to a PDF + short email template for CS outreach. Could we also make a one-paragraph 'what this solves' for execs?
Sam (SRE): I'll add that. I'll push updated draft here by EOD.
deploy-bot: Deployed draft to docs staging at https://docs-staging.redwood.ai/cs/surge-cheatsheet (preview)
Kyle (Support): Preview looks good. Tag me when it's final so we can attach to the customer onboarding template. :white_check_mark:
